'''''Acer pseudosieboldianum''''', the '''Korean maple''' or '''purplebloom maple''', is a species of [[maple]]. It is native to northeastern [[China]], [[Korea]], and the [[Russian Far East]].<ref name=hok>Hokanson, S. [http://www.extension.umn.edu/yardandgarden/YGLNews/YGLN-Sept1503.html ''Acer pseudosieboldianum'' - A Japanese-like maple for the North?] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322132515/http://www.extension.umn.edu/yardandgarden/YGLNews/YGLN-Sept1503.html |date=March 22, 2012 }} ''Yard & Garden Line News'' 5(15) September 15, 2003. University of Minnesota Extension.</ref><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 19 January 2018}}</ref>

==Description==
''Acer pseudosieboldianum'' is a small [[tree]] or [[shrub]]. It is [[deciduous]]. It grows about 12 to 18 inches per year. The mature tree is 15 to 25 feet tall.<ref>[http://www.bcarboretum.org/CulturalInfo.aspx?VCID=803 Cultural Details for ''Acer pseudosieboldianum''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905043835/http://www.bcarboretum.org/CulturalInfo.aspx?VCID=803 |date=2011-09-05 }} Boone County Arboretum. Union, Kentucky, USA.</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242300464 Flora of China, ''Acer pseudosieboldianum'' (Pax) Komarov, 1904.  <big>紫花枫</big> zi hua feng ]</ref>

The leaves are 4 to 6 inches wide and have usually 9 to 11 lobes. The green leaves turn shades of red, yellow, and orange in fall. This species exhibits [[Marcescence]] (tends to hold on to a portion of its dried leaves through the winter). The flowers are white with purple [[bract]]s. New growth is coated in white, sticky hairs. This characteristic distinguishes the plant from the similar ''[[Acer sieboldianum]]'', which lacks hairs.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/16154925#page/737/mode/1up Komarov, Vladimir Leontjevich 1904.  Trudy Imperatorskago S.-Peterburgskago Botaničeskago Sada 22: 725-727] in Russian</ref>

The [[Bark (botany)|bark]] of the plant is thin and easily damaged by mechanical injury or in harsh weather. Tears in the bark make it vulnerable to insect and [[fungus|fungal]] infestation. The species is susceptible to [[canker]] and [[Verticillium wilt]] when stressed.

==Uses==
The Korean maple is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]]. It withstands a cold climate better than the comparable [[Acer palmatum|Japanese maple]]. It has been grown in [[North Dakota]], where it has done well in temperatures as low −43 °F.<ref name=hok/> The species has been hybridized with Japanese Maple at the [[University of Wisconsin]] to produce a cold hardy tree with intermediate characteristics between the two parents. This hybrid has been named ''Acer pseudosieboldianum'' × ''palmatum'' 'Hasselkus' and marketed under the trade name Northern Glow®.
